events.title: THE HOUSEHOLD PROTOCOLS CONTINUE THROUGH THE SPRING WORKING WEEK
events.body: The household begins the week under the same instructions Valerius has already established: inspections are to be performed without needless harshness, stores are to be accounted for, and workers encountered during the rounds are to be treated with respect. Stewards move between the principal stores, work areas, and field boundaries while the longer spring days increase the pressure on every part of the estate. Small discrepancies in tools and assignments are corrected before they become disputes, and the work rolls are brought into closer agreement with the actual labor being performed. The routine is orderly rather than ceremonial, but its repetition is becoming part of the household's ordinary administration. By the end of the day's rounds, the estate's records remain coherent and the standing instructions continue without interruption.

events.title: THE RAID DOSSIER IS CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST AN OLDER HOUSEHOLD ENTRY
events.body: The continuing inquiry into the earlier raid reaches another documentary comparison within the household archive. A notation associated with Aulus Vettius is brought beside the authenticated copies already prepared for Roman review, and the scribes distinguish the original entry from later recollection rather than allowing the two to become a single account. The comparison does not settle every question, but it identifies which portion of the record can be treated as contemporary household documentation. A second copy is marked for reference should the Roman correspondence return with another request. The archive therefore grows more useful not by adding a dramatic new accusation, but by making the existing evidence easier to examine.

events.title: A SMALLHOLDER ARRIVES WITH A SECOND ACCOUNT OF THE OLD ROUTE
events.body: A smallholder from beyond the newer tract arrives with an account concerning the old route that had figured in the estate's earlier inquiries. He does not present it as a formal accusation, but as a practical recollection of where people once passed when the boundary country was less settled. His description overlaps with part of the testimony already preserved, while differing on one turn in the route. The stewards record the distinction instead of forcing the account into the existing version. Valerius's archive therefore gains another small piece of information whose value lies precisely in the fact that it can be compared rather than simply accepted.

events.title: THE PURCHASED FIELDS COMPLETE ANOTHER HEAVY DAY OF SPRING WORK
events.body: The purchased tract now works alongside the older fields without the distinction of ownership disrupting the ordinary rhythm of the estate. Laborers clear, turn, and tend the ground according to the condition of each plot, while stewards keep the newer acreage visible in the work records. The additional ground consumes more provisions during the long working days, and the household stores are drawn upon accordingly. No new land is acquired and no boundary is altered; the work is the continuation of the tract's first full season under Valerius's administration. By evening the fields have advanced another stage, but the week's increased labor has left the stores somewhat tighter than they were at its beginning.

events.title: THE LAKE-PORT MERCHANTS CONFIRM THAT THE SPRING LOADS HAVE REACHED THE NEXT STAGE OF TRANSIT
events.body: Word returns from the merchant connection that the spring loads prepared at the estate have entered the next stage of their journey toward the lake-port trade route. The message concerns movement and timing rather than payment, and the estate keeps the commercial records separate from household provisions as before. Merchant agents confirm the quantities already prepared and ask that future correspondence continue through the same channel. The exchange strengthens the practical connection between the estate's spring production and its established merchant network. No new financial receipt is recorded from the message itself, because the surviving account does not establish a completed payment at this point.

events.title: METELLUS CELER'S CORRESPONDENCE KEEPS THE EXPEDITION RECORD WITHIN ROMAN POLITICAL CIRCULATION
events.body: A further Roman communication keeps Valerius's recent expedition within the circle of political correspondence already established around his affairs. Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer is represented in the continuing correspondence, while the household scribes preserve the expedition account separately from the older raid dossier. The distinction matters: the expedition record concerns observations made for Roman authorities, whereas the raid papers remain an evidentiary archive under separate review. The two documentary threads now sit beside one another without being confused. The exchange leaves Valerius's Roman connections active as the household continues its ordinary spring administration.

events.title: THE WEEKLY RECORDS CLOSE WITH THE TWO INVESTIGATIVE THREADS KEPT DISTINCT
events.body: At week's end the household scribes close the current records and preserve the expedition account, the raid dossier, and the ordinary estate papers as distinct documentary sets. Marcus Claudius Marcellus's earlier questions remain attached to the raid material, while the correspondence associated with Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer remains with the broader Roman exchange. The arrangement prevents the extraordinary expedition from obscuring the older inquiry and prevents the older inquiry from being mistaken for the purpose of the expedition. Copies are sealed, dated, and returned to the household archive for further use. The estate enters the next week with its spring work continuing and its documentary obligations more clearly organized than they were at the beginning of the season.
